rootCauseAnalysis.summary: The CDIDefaultStorageClassDegraded alert is firing because the default StorageClass 'lvms-vg1' (provisioner: topolvm.io) does not support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode, making it unsuitable as a KubeVirt/CDI virtual machine default storage class — it is the Kubernetes default but not the KubeVirt virt default.
causalChain: Signal: CDIDefaultStorageClassDegraded alert fires on StorageProfile for lvms-vg1
Why? CDI reports kubevirt_cdi_storageprofile_info{degraded=true, default=true, rwx=false, virtdefault=false} = 1

Why? StorageClass lvms-vg1 is the Kubernetes default (storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: true) but lacks RWX support — StorageProfile claimPropertySets only contain ReadWriteOnce access modes
Why? lvms-vg1 uses the topolvm.io (LVMS/LVM) provisioner which provides node-local block storage — architecturally incapable of RWX without a shared filesystem overlay

Root cause: No RWX-capable StorageClass exists that is designated as the KubeVirt virt-default (storageclass.kubevirt.io/is-default-virt-class: true), so CDI falls back to the Kubernetes default (lvms-vg1) which is RWO-only, triggering the degraded alert

dueDiligence.targetAccuracy: The StorageClass lvms-vg1 is the resource whose annotation configuration needs to change (either adding storageclass.kubevirt.io/is-default-virt-class: true to an RWX-capable class, or the StorageProfile needs a claimPropertySet for RWX). However, since lvms-vg1 physically cannot provide RWX, the actual fix may require adding a new RWX-capable StorageClass and annotating it as virtdefault. StorageClass lvms-vg1 is targeted as the degraded resource per Prometheus evidence.
dueDiligence.proportionality: The remediation target (StorageClass lvms-vg1) is the specific resource causing the degradation. The fix is targeted: either annotate an RWX-capable class as virt-default, or accept the architectural limitation. The memory-eater OOMKill is listed as a contributing factor but is a separate issue with its own remediation (increase memory limit or fix the workload).
dueDiligence.scopeCompleteness: Checked: StorageClass lvms-vg1 (YAML+annotations), StorageProfile lvms-vg1 (spec+status), CDIConfig (spec+status), Prometheus kubevirt_cdi_storageprofile_info metric, Deployment/memory-eater, Pod/memory-eater-85c4d9667b-4q8pg (describe+events+logs), PVCs in namespace (none). Did not check VolumeSnapshotClass or individual LVMCluster resources — not relevant to RWX capability determination.
dueDiligence.causalCompleteness: Traced from alert -> Prometheus metric -> StorageProfile degraded=true -> RWX not supported -> LVMS node-local architecture -> no virt-default class designated. Cannot go deeper without inspecting the LVMCluster resource or hardware RAID/network storage configuration.
dueDiligence.evidenceSufficiency: All claims backed by: (1) Prometheus kubevirt_cdi_storageprofile_info metric showing degraded=true, rwx=false, virtdefault=false; (2) StorageClass YAML showing only RWO access in StorageProfile claimPropertySets; (3) CDIConfig showing scratchSpaceStorageClass=lvms-vg1; (4) Pod events confirming OOMKilled for memory-eater as a separate unrelated issue. No inaccessible data sources for this alert.
dueDiligence.regressionAwareness: No prior remediation history available for StorageClass/lvms-vg1 or StorageProfile/lvms-vg1 per get_cluster_resource_context output.
dueDiligence.alternativeHypotheses: Considered: (1) CDI operator misconfiguration — ruled out, CDI v4.18.43 is running, cdi-deployment pod is healthy (metrics being scraped). (2) Missing StorageProfile entirely — ruled out, StorageProfile/lvms-vg1 exists and is fully populated. (3) Filesystem overhead issue — ruled out, filesystemOverhead is configured at 0.06 in CDIConfig. (4) VolumeBindingMode incompatibility — WaitForFirstConsumer is supported by CDI via HonorWaitForFirstConsumer feature gate which is enabled. The rwx=false label is the direct discriminator.
dueDiligence.confidenceCalibration: Starting at 1.0. -0.05 for not verifying whether a separate RWX-capable StorageClass exists but was not designated as virt-default (only one StorageClass found in cluster). -0.05 for not being able to inspect the LVMCluster resource directly to confirm hardware-level RWX impossibility. Final confidence: 0.90.

contributingFactors: StorageClass lvms-vg1 only supports ReadWriteOnce (Block and Filesystem) — no RWX support means VMs cannot live-migrate

StorageClass lvms-vg1 is annotated as the Kubernetes default (storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: true) but lacks the KubeVirt virt-default annotation (storageclass.kubevirt.io/is-default-virt-class: true)
CDI StorageProfile for lvms-vg1 reports virtdefault=false and rwx=false while default=true and degraded=true
LVM Storage (topolvm.io) inherently does not support RWX volumes without a shared filesystem layer
CDIConfig uses lvms-vg1 as scratchSpaceStorageClass, further coupling CDI operations to this degraded profile
Deployment/memory-eater in the signal namespace is separately in CrashLoopBackOff due to intentional OOMKilled behavior (50Mi memory limit, allocating 5MB/s), unrelated to the CDI alert

kaResponse.analysis: The CDIDefaultStorageClassDegraded alert is firing because the default StorageClass 'lvms-vg1' (provisioner: topolvm.io) does not support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode, making it unsuitable as a KubeVirt/CDI virtual machine default storage class — it is the Kubernetes default but not the KubeVirt virt default.
